subject.title: v2026.6.8: plugin_state_entries SQLite database corruption — session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released

question: Should OpenClaw add availability-first shared SQLite corruption recovery for openclaw.sqlite now, or first require proof that EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError can cause the plugin-state corruption?
rationale: The code boundary is clear, but the right fix changes shared persisted-state recovery, data-retention semantics, WAL/checkpoint policy, and session-lock ownership across multiple runtime surfaces.

options.title: Define shared-state recovery first
options.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement it with plugin-state and task-state regression proof while continuing the session-lock RCA.

options.title: Prove causality first
options.body: Keep fail-closed runtime behavior while maintainers collect malformed DB sidecars, integrity traces, and a live current-main takeover-to-corruption reproduction.

options.title: Split into existing trackers
options.body: Close this only if maintainers decide the task-registry malformed SQLite thread and narrower session-takeover issues fully own the remaining work.

recommendation.title: Define shared-state recovery first
recommendation.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement it with plugin-state and task-state regression proof while continuing the session-lock RCA.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the shared SQLite boundary is the database-first refactor and plugin-state migration introduced through the SQLite runtime work.
